name: Satin-Furnace
specific_features: Obsidian fields that reflect the sky like satin fabric
Thermophilic bacterial colonies coloring lava flows crimson
description: Satin-Furnace earns its name from the vast obsidian plains that cover nearly a third of its surface, cooled lava flows polished by constant volcanic ashfall into surfaces so smooth they reflect the perpetually orange sky like dark satin. Rivers of molten rock wind between these glass fields, fed by a chain of hyperactive volcanoes along the planet's primary tectonic fault line. The planet is geologically young and furiously active, reshaping itself on timescales measured in decades rather than millennia.

The atmosphere is a choking mixture of sulfur dioxide, carbon dioxide, and volcanic particulates that turns the sky into a permanent burnt-orange haze. Visibility rarely exceeds a few hundred meters, and the air temperature can spike without warning when subsurface magma chambers shift. The toxic soup would kill an unprotected human in seconds, yet life has found a way. Thermophilic microorganisms thrive in the boundary zones where cooling lava meets volcanic gases, painting the margins of lava flows in vivid reds and oranges.

Mining surveys have identified extraordinarily rich deposits of platinum group metals concentrated in the volcanic calderas, likely brought to the surface by the planet's intense geological churning. The obsidian itself has properties that make it valuable for precision optical instruments, as its purity exceeds anything producible in laboratories. Early robotic extraction operations proved profitable but short-lived, as the constantly shifting terrain destroyed equipment faster than it could be replaced.

The discovery of native microbial life complicated extraction plans further, as contamination protocols now apply to all surface operations. The microbes themselves are of significant scientific interest, representing a form of biochemistry based partially on silicon rather than carbon. Several xenobiochemistry firms have expressed interest in securing research rights, seeing potential applications in high-temperature industrial processes. Satin-Furnace burns and reshapes itself endlessly, indifferent to the plans being made for its riches.
